mainTopic: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's teachings about ספק ממזר and marriage, then inheritance disputes over a child of doubtful father after יבום, and whether an old verdict stands or is reopened.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: הלכתא אהלכתא, two separate rulings stacked together. אביי then tries to prove that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב treats a ספק ממזר like a definite ממזר, using a ברייתא about children of unknown fathers. רבא pushes the proof off by reading זמה as 'זו מה היא', 'what is this?', which describes doubt rather than certainty. The same ברייתא warns a man not to marry wives in two countries. The גמרא asks how רב and רב נחמן could take wives on their travels, and answers that famous rabbis are different. It then explains how they handled שבעה נקיים, and adds רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule against marrying with a plan to divorce. Next come inheritance cases about a child who may be the son of the dead brother or of the יבם. Against the יבם, money in doubt is split. רב משרשיא shows that the 'bring proof and take' rule applies only when the other side's claim is certain. Finally, רבי אבא and רבי ירמיה argue whether an old verdict stands or is reopened. The גמרא compares this to the argument between אדמון and the חכמים about a lost path, a comparison that is still being worked out on the next amud.

steps.title: A ruling on top of a ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion by explaining that two rulings were stated, one on top of the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is one הלכה on top of another הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question from just before this point, about why a ruling was needed. It says this is one הלכה stacked on another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate rulings are being given. One says the הלכה follows רב in this specific case. The other says the הלכה generally follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The second ruling does not make the first one unnecessary, because each teaches something of its own.
steps.confusionAlert: This short line closes the earlier discussion. It is not the start of אביי's new topic that comes next.

phrases.english: A halakha on top of a halakha.
phrases.notes: He means there are two rulings: one for this specific case, and one general rule to follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.triggerLanguage: הלכתא אהלכתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question raised before this section begins, about why a separate ruling was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both rulings are needed; they are two separate rulings, one stacked on the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rulings stand: one for this specific case and one general rule.

steps.title: אביי's claim: a doubt counts as a certainty
steps.stepSummary: אביי announces that, for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, any ספק ממזר is treated like a definite ממזר, and says he will prove it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know that, for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, every doubtful case is treated like a certain one?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי states his opinion about how רבי אליעזר בן יעקב views a ספק ממזר. This step sets up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a ספק (doubt) is not the same as a ודאי (certainty). אביי says that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב treats someone who might be a ממזר exactly like someone who definitely is one. The words 'מנא אמינא לה' tell us a source is about to be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (a proof is coming)
He makes it equal to / treats it as

phrases.english: Abaye said:
From where do I say it

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֹל סְפֵיקָא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב —
phrases.english: that every doubtful case, according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
he treats it like a certainty,

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי מנא אמינא לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about how רבי אליעזר בן יעקב views a ספק ממזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a ספק ממזר is treated as a definite ממזר.

steps.title: The proof: the world filled with ממזרין
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר בן יעקב warns that children of unknown fathers could marry close relatives, and he calls the result 'ממזרין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: A man had relations with many women and does not know which of them he had relations with. Likewise, a woman had relations with many men and does not know from which one she conceived. The result could be that a father marries his daughter and a brother marries his sister, and the whole world fills up with ממזרין. About this the פסוק says: 'And the land will become full of זמה.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings his proof. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב calls the possible result 'ממזרין', even though no one knows for sure that any particular child is one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every child born in this situation is only possibly the product of a forbidden relationship, so each one is only a ספק. Still, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the world fills with 'ממזרין' and does not say 'ספק ממזרין'. אביי concludes that he treats the doubt as a certainty.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
She received (the seed), meaning she became pregnant
ממזרים, children of a forbidden relationship

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the main source that will be read in two different ways: as speaking about certainty (אביי) or about doubt (רבא).

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
One who had relations with many women

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין יוֹדֵעַ עַל אֵיזוֹ מֵהֶן בָּא,
phrases.english: and does not know which of them he had relations with,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הִיא שֶׁבָּאוּ עָלֶיהָ אֲנָשִׁים הַרְבֵּה,
phrases.english: and likewise a woman with whom many men had relations,
and she does not know from which of them she conceived —
it turns out that a father may marry his daughter,
and a brother may marry his sister,
and the entire world becomes filled with mamzerim.
phrases.notes: This word is אביי's proof: he says 'ממזרין' and not 'ספק ממזרין'.

phrases.english: And about this it is said:
"And the land become full of lewdness."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:29

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא רבי אליעזר בן יעקב אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that אביי promised in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב treats a ספק ממזר as a definite ממזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב that calls children of unknown fathers 'ממזרין' and quotes 'ומלאה הארץ זמה'.

steps.title: רבא: זמה means 'what is this?'
steps.stepSummary: רבא pushes away the proof by reading the word זמה as 'זו מה היא', meaning 'what is this?'. That reading describes doubt, not certainty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא would tell you: this is what the פסוק is saying: 'זו מה היא', 'what is this?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects אביי's proof. The פסוק that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב quoted actually shows the children are a question mark, not definite ממזרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא splits the word זמה into 'זו מה היא', 'what is this one?'. That is the language of confusion: no one knows who is who. So the ברייתא may be calling them ספק ממזרים, and it cannot prove that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב treats a ספק as a ודאי.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (a reply that pushes off the proof)
What is this? (a play on the word זמה)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי reads the ברייתא as calling these children definite ממזרים, so a ספק counts as a ודאי. רבא reads זמה as 'זו מה היא', 'what is this?', so the children are only in doubt and the proof falls away.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying these children are permitted or that nothing is wrong. He is only saying their status is a doubt, not a certainty.

phrases.english: And Rava would say to you,
this is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the פסוק that the ברייתא quoted, 'ומלאה הארץ זמה'.

phrases.english: "What is this one?"
phrases.notes: He reads the word זמה as three words, זו מה היא: nobody can tell what this child's status is.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבא אמר לך הכי קאמר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not settle the question for certain either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק's word זמה can be read as 'זו מה היא', which describes doubt. So the ברייתא does not have to mean definite ממזרים.

steps.title: Do not marry wives in two different countries
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says a man should not marry one wife in one country and another wife in a different country, because their children might marry each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב said: A man should not marry a woman in one country and then go and marry another woman in a different country. The children might pair up with each other, and a brother would end up marrying his sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He adds a second warning, this time about how a man arranges his own marriages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the ברייתא he worried about children whose father is unknown. Here he goes further. Even with a known father, two families living far apart might not know about each other, so a half-brother and half-sister could marry by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest they pair up (marry each other)

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן, אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: Furthermore, Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִשָּׂא אָדָם אִשָּׁה בִּמְדִינָה זוֹ
phrases.english: A man should not marry a woman in this country
and then go and marry a woman in another country,
lest they pair up with one another,
phrases.notes: "They" means the children, a son from one wife and a daughter from the other, who don't know they share a father.

phrases.english: and it turns out that a brother marries his sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן, אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 3, adding a second, wider warning from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man should not marry wives in two different countries, because his children from each might unknowingly marry each other.

steps.title: But רב and רב נחמן married wives in other towns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's warning: רב in דרדשיר and רב נחמן in שכנציב each announced, 'Who will be my wife for the day?'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But when רב came to דרדשיר, he announced: 'Who will be my wife for the time I am here?' And when רב נחמן came to שכנציב, he also announced: 'Who will be my wife for the time I am here?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether this warning is really the rule. Two great אמוראים married temporary wives while away from home, which looks like exactly what רבי אליעזר בן יעקב warned against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רב and רב נחמן already had wives at home and took another wife in a different town. If the warning were binding, these great rabbis would not have done this. So their behavior seems to show there is no such rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Who will be [my wife] for the day?

phrases.english: Is that so?
But Rav, when he happened to come to Dardeshir,
announced and said: Who will be [my wife] for the day?
phrases.notes: "For the day" means for the length of his stay. The word in square brackets belongs to the corrected wording.

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman, when he happened to come to Shakhnetziv,
announced and said: Who will be [my wife] for the day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַב כִּי אִיקְּלַע לְדַרְדְּשִׁיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the warning just given in step 5 using the actual behavior of two אמוראים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's warning not to marry wives in two different countries.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Great rabbis did exactly this, so it seems there is no such rule.

steps.title: Rabbis are different because everyone knows their children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבנן are different: their names are famous, so their children will always be known as theirs, and no sibling mix-up will happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן are different, because their names are well known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's warning by saying it does not apply to famous rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that the children would not know they share a father. A famous rabbi's children are always known as 'the son of so-and-so' or 'the daughter of so-and-so,' so nobody would let them marry each other. The warning stays in place for ordinary people.

phrases.english: Rabbis are different,
since their names are well known.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַבָּנַן, דִּפְקִיעַ שְׁמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by showing that the cases of רב and רב נחמן are an exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק): famous rabbis versus ordinary people
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stories of רב and רב נחמן show there is no rule against marrying in two countries.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stands, but it does not apply to famous rabbis, whose children are always known as theirs.
steps.whatToRemember: The reason behind the warning is that the children won't know who their father is. Where that can't happen, as with famous rabbis, the warning doesn't apply.

steps.title: How could they marry the same day if the woman needs seven clean days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new problem with the stories: רבא said a woman who agrees to marry must count שבעה נקיים, so how could רב and רב נחמן marry on arrival?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא say: If a woman was asked to marry and she agreed, she must wait seven clean days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the stories of רב and רב נחמן from a different angle. It is setting up a problem, and the answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא teaches that a woman who agrees to marry must count שבעה נקיים before living with her husband, because the excitement may have caused bleeding. If so, the rabbis could not have married a woman as soon as they arrived in town. The challenge is now about the timing in the stories, not about רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's rule.
steps.confusionAlert: This question is no longer about marrying in two countries. It asks how רב and רב נחמן could marry so quickly, given רבא's rule of seven clean days.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:
If they asked her to marry and she agreed,
she must wait seven clean days?
phrases.notes: "Clean" means days with no sign of bleeding. Only after them may she live with her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רָבָא: תְּבָעוּהָ לִינָּשֵׂא וְנִתְפַּיְּיסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the stories in step 6 and questions how they could have happened at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The stories of רב and רב נחמן, who announced 'Who will be my wife for the day?'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא requires seven clean days after a woman agrees to marry, so a short visit would not allow time for such a marriage.

steps.title: The Rabbis sent messengers ahead of time
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן sent messengers in advance to let the woman know they were coming, so she had time to count שבעה נקיים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן would send their messengers ahead, and they would let the women know.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 8: the רבנן did not really marry the woman by surprise on the day they arrived. They sent word ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a woman who agrees to marry must first count שבעה נקיים, so a same-day wedding seems impossible. If she was told days earlier, she already finished counting by the time the רב arrived. So the stories of רב and רב נחמן fit with רבא's rule after all.

keyTerms.meaning: seven clean days a woman counts before marriage

phrases.english: The Rabbis, their messengers
they would send, and they would inform them.
phrases.notes: They sent word ahead, so the woman had time to count her seven clean days before the רב arrived.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן שְׁלוּחַיְיהוּ הֲווֹ מְשַׁדְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by adding a fact about how the marriages happened.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual clarification: the woman was told ahead of time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן married women the same day they arrived, with no time for שבעה נקיים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Messengers announced their coming beforehand, so the seven days were already counted.

steps.title: The Rabbis only wanted seclusion, not relations
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the רבנן only meant to be secluded with the woman, which needs no שבעה נקיים. Just knowing a wife is available calms desire.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: for the רבנן, it was just being alone together that they did with them. As מר said: someone who has bread in his basket is not like someone who has no bread in his basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question from step 8. The רבנן married only to be secluded with the wife, not to have relations, so counting seven days was not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule about שבעה נקיים only matters if the couple will have relations. If the רבנן only wanted ייחוד, the rule does not stop the marriage. The proof is a saying: a hungry person with bread in his basket feels calmer, so a man who knows he has a wife is calmer too.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say (introduces another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to the question about רב and רב נחמן: they announced their coming early, or they wanted only seclusion, because having a wife available calms desire.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
for the Rabbis, merely seclusion
is what they would have with them,
phrases.notes: Literally, "they would be alone with them." Being alone together is the whole point, with no relations.

phrases.english: as the Master said:
one who has is not comparable,
bread in his basket,
to one who has no bread in his basket.
phrases.notes: Knowing food is there eases hunger. In the same way, knowing he has a wife eases a man's desire.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְרַבָּנַן, יַחוֹדֵי בְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the same קשיא answered in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the purpose of the marriage: seclusion only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The marriage meant relations right away, which needs שבעה נקיים first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The marriage was only for ייחוד, which brings peace of mind and needs no waiting.

steps.title: Do not marry while planning to divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב teaches that a man should not marry a woman while already planning to divorce her. He learns this from a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, a man should not marry his wife while his mind is set on divorcing her, because it says: "Do not plan evil against your friend while he lives trustingly with you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the same תנא from step 5. He forbids marrying with a hidden plan to divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife trusts that the marriage is real and lasting. Secretly planning to end it is "plotting evil" against someone who feels safe with you, as the פסוק in משלי says.

keyTerms.meaning: his intention is to divorce her
do not plot, do not plan

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a moral rule: marriage must not be entered with a secret plan to break the wife's trust.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
A man should not marry his wife
while his intention is to divorce her,
because it is stated:
"Do not plot evil against your neighbor,
while he dwells securely with you."
phrases.notes: משלי 3:29

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: לֹא יִשָּׂא אָדָם אִשְׁתּוֹ וְדַעְתּוֹ לְגָרְשָׁהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא teaching of the same תנא quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man may not marry a woman while secretly intending to divorce her, based on משלי 3:29.

steps.title: A doubtful son and the יבם both claim the inheritance
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a child who may be the son of the dead brother or of the יבם fights the יבם over the dead man's property. Each one claims all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A doubtful son and a יבם came to divide the property of the dead man. The doubtful one said: I am the dead man's son, and the property is mine. The יבם said: You are my son, and you have nothing at all in the property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic from the משנה: the child born seven months after יבום. It sets up the inheritance fight before giving the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know if the baby came from the first husband, born at nine months, or from the יבם, born at seven months. If he is the dead man's son, he inherits his father. If he is the יבם's son, the יבם inherits his brother through יבום, and the child gets nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: a doubtful one: a child whose father is uncertain
the brother who did יבום with the widow
the property of the dead man

steps.confusionAlert: Both people say "the property is mine." The child does not claim to be the יבם's son. Each side is making the claim that helps himself.

phrases.english: A doubtful one and a yavam
phrases.notes: This is the baby from the משנה born seven months after יבום. He could belong to either husband.

phrases.english: who came to divide the property of the deceased,
the doubtful one said:
I am the son of the deceased,
and the property is mine.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some have the word in square brackets. Both mean "they are."

phrases.english: And the yavam said:
You are my own son,
and you have nothing at all in the property.
phrases.notes: Through יבום the יבם inherits his brother. So if the child is his, the child has no share.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק וְיָבָם שֶׁבָּאוּ לַחֲלוֹק בְּנִכְסֵי מִיתָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and starts a new case based on the משנה's seven-month child.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the doubtful son and the יבם each claim the whole inheritance.

steps.title: Money in doubt is split
steps.stepSummary: Since we cannot know who the rightful heir is, this is ממון המוטל בספק, and such money is divided between the two sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is money in doubt, and money in doubt is divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the ruling for the case set up in step 12: the doubtful son and the יבם split the property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side can prove his claim, and there is no way to find out the truth. In such a case, money placed in doubt is shared between the two claimants instead of all going to one.

keyTerms.meaning: money placed in doubt: property whose owner cannot be determined

steps.whatToRemember: When a ספק son and a יבם both claim the dead man's property, the rule of ממון המוטל בספק applies, and they split it.

phrases.english: It is money placed in doubt,
and money placed in doubt, they divide.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי מָמוֹן הַמּוּטָּל בְּסָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the dispute set up in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Property whose rightful owner cannot be known is split between the claimants. So the doubtful son and the יבם each take half.

steps.title: The doubtful son versus the sons of the יבם
steps.stepSummary: A new case: the ספק claims all the dead man's property as his only son. The יבם's sons say he is their brother and gets only a share with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A child whose father is uncertain and the sons of the יבם came to divide the dead man's property. The doubtful one said: 'I am the son of the dead man, so the property is mine.' The sons of the יבם said: 'You are our brother, so you only have a share together with us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a second dispute about the same kind of doubtful child. This time his opponents are the sons of the יבם, not the יבם himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last case (Step 12) the ספק argued with the יבם. Now the יבם's sons are the ones arguing. If the ספק is the dead man's son, he takes everything. If he is the יבם's son, the property passed to the יבם and is now split among all the יבם's sons, so he gets only a share.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubtful one. Here, a child who could be the son of the dead brother or of the יבם
The sons of the brother who did יבום

phrases.english: A doubtful one and the sons of the יבם
who came to divide the property of the dead man,
the doubtful one said:
"That man is the son of the dead man,
phrases.notes: "That man" is just a polite way of saying "I". He is talking about himself.

phrases.english: and the property is mine."
phrases.notes: Some versions say הוּא, in round brackets; the corrected wording has נִינְהוּ, in square brackets. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: The sons of the יבם say:
"You are our brother,
phrases.notes: Some versions say אַחֵינוּ and some say אֲחוּנָא. Both mean "our brother".

phrases.english: and you only have a share together with us."

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק וּבְנֵי יָבָם שֶׁבָּאוּ לַחֲלוֹק בְּנִכְסֵי מִיתָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling on the ספק versus the יבם (Step 13), the גמרא brings a parallel case with the יבם's sons as the other side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the dispute. The ספק claims all of the property, and the יבם's sons claim he gets only a share.

steps.title: The students think a משנה settles this case
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן in front of רב משרשיא suggest the case is already covered by a משנה: the doubtful son does not inherit from the others, but they inherit from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן sitting before רב משרשיא wanted to say: This case is our משנה, as we learned: 'He does not inherit them, but they inherit him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The students try to answer the new case by pointing to a משנה. This step only quotes the משנה. The next step explains how it fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about a different kind of doubtful child, one who might belong to either of two husbands. When one of the other brothers dies, the doubtful child cannot take from his estate. When the doubtful child dies, the others do inherit from him. The students think the same logic will decide our case.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis thought (at first). This often signals an idea that may later be rejected
An אמורא in whose presence the students were learning
It is (already taught in) our משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'he' and 'them' in the quoted משנה are not the people in our case. 'He' is a doubtful child of two possible husbands, and 'them' are the sons of those husbands. The students are only comparing the two cases.

phrases.aramaic: סְבוּר רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לְמֵימַר:
phrases.english: The Rabbis before רב משרשיא thought to say:
It is our משנה,
as we learned:
He does not inherit them,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה later in יבמות about a baby who might be from the first husband or the second.

phrases.english: but they inherit him.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבוּר רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לְמֵימַר מַתְנִיתִין הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to decide the case from Step 14 using an existing משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Who wins the dispute between the ספק and the יבם's sons
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'He does not inherit them, but they inherit him.'

steps.title: Same rule, with the sides switched
steps.stepSummary: The students explain how the משנה applies. There, the brothers tell the doubtful one to bring proof. Here, the doubtful one tells the יבם's sons to bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here it is the other way around. There, they say to him: 'Bring proof and take.' Here, he says to them: 'Bring proof and take.'
steps.whatsHappening: The students finish their comparison. They say the משנה's rule fits our case, but the roles are reversed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared rule is that whoever holds the solid claim can say, 'Bring proof and then take.' In the משנה, the brothers have the solid claim, so the doubtful one gets nothing without proof. Here, the ספק surely inherits something either way, so the students hold that the יבם's sons are the ones who must prove he is not the dead man's son.

keyTerms.meaning: The reverse, the other way around
There (in the משנה) / here (in our case)
Bring proof and take. You must prove your claim before you can collect

steps.whatToRemember: The students' idea: the ספק keeps everything unless the יבם's sons prove he is not the dead man's son. This is the reverse of the משנה, where the doubtful one is the side that must bring proof.

phrases.english: And here it is the other way around.
There, they say to him:
"Bring proof and take,"
here, he says to them:
"Bring proof and take."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכָא אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in Step 15 applies to the case in Step 14, with the sides switched.
steps.raayaObject: That the ספק keeps the property unless the יבם's sons bring proof
steps.raayaSupportSource: The 'bring proof and take' logic of the משנה, applied in reverse

steps.title: רב משרשיא says the two cases are not alike
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא rejects the comparison to the משנה. There, one side is certain and the other doubtful. Here, both sides are doubtful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said to them: Are the cases really alike? There, they are certain and he is doubtful. Here, both sides are doubtful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא pushes back on the רבנן. He says the משנה they brought is not the same as our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the brothers are surely brothers of the one who died, so their claim is sure, and the ספק must bring proof. In our case, the יבם's sons can only claim through the idea that the ספק is their brother, and that is itself doubtful. When both sides are doubtful, 'bring proof' cannot be used to push one side out.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they alike? A way of saying 'the cases are not the same'
doubtful, an unsure claim (also the name for the son whose father is unknown)
this one and that one, both sides

steps.confusionAlert: The rule 'bring proof and take' only works when the other side has a sure claim. It is not a general rule that the ספק always loses.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the רבנן from steps 15-16 who compared our case to the משנה.

phrases.english: Are they alike?
There, they are certain and he is doubtful.
Here, both this one and that one are doubtful.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם, אִינְהוּ וַדַּאי וְאִיהוּ סָפֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof the רבנן brought from the משנה in steps 15-16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between the משנה and the case of step 14.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the משנה, one side's claim is sure. In our case, both claims are doubtful, so the 'bring proof' rule does not apply.

steps.title: The case the משנה really fits
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא says the משנה matches a different case: the ספק and the יבם's sons dividing the יבם's own property, where the sons can say 'bring proof that you are our brother.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if any case is like the משנה, it is this one: a ספק and the יבם's sons who come to divide the property of the יבם himself. There they can say to him: Bring proof that you are our brother, and then take.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the comparison, רב משרשיא names the case the משנה does fit. That is the יבם's own estate, not the dead brother's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the יבם's own property, the יבם's sons are surely his sons, so their claim is sure. The ספק can only share if he is the יבם's son, and that is doubtful. So, just like the משנה, they can tell him to bring proof, and without proof he gets nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows exactly when the 'bring proof' rule works: only when the other side's claim is sure.

phrases.english: Rather, if it is alike to the משנה
it is alike to this:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: to a doubtful one and the יבם's sons
who came to divide the property of the יבם himself,
for there they say to him:
Bring proof that you are our brother, and take.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִי דָּמְיָא לְמַתְנִיתִין לְהָא דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the comparison in step 17, gives the correct case the משנה matches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a fight over the יבם's own property, the יבם's sons have a sure claim, and the ספק must prove he is their brother before he gets a share.
steps.whatToRemember: Dead brother's property: both sides are doubtful, so they split it. The יבם's own property: the sons are sure, so the ספק needs proof.

steps.title: A new case: the יבם's estate after he already split the dead man's property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a new case. The ספק and the יבם's sons come to divide the יבם's estate, after the יבם had already split the dead brother's property with the ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A doubtful one and the יבם's sons who came to divide the יבם's property, after the יבם had divided the dead man's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new, harder case. The claims of each side come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in step 13, the יבם and the ספק split the dead brother's property, since it was ממון המוטל בספק. Now the יבם has died. His estate includes the half he took from the dead brother. That detail is what makes this case new.

keyTerms.meaning: the dead man (the brother who died without children)

phrases.english: A doubtful one and the יבם's sons
who came to divide the יבם's property,
after the יבם had divided the dead man's property,
phrases.notes: This is the split from step 13. The יבם and the ספק each took half of the dead brother's estate.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק וּבְנֵי יָבָם שֶׁבָּאוּ לַחְלוֹק בְּנִכְסֵי יָבָם, לְבָתַר דִּפְלַג יָבָם בְּנִכְסֵי מִיתָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 18's case (the יבם's own property) and adds that the יבם already split the dead man's estate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case only. No ruling is given yet.

steps.title: The two sides' claims: 'bring proof' against 'whichever way you look at it'
steps.stepSummary: The יבם's sons tell the ספק to prove he is their brother. The ספק answers that either way he deserves something: a brother's share, or the half their father took from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The יבם's sons say: Bring proof that you are our brother, and take. The doubtful one said to them: Whichever way you want it, if I am your brother, give me a share with you. And if I am the dead man's son, give me the half that your father divided with me.
steps.whatsHappening: Each side states its claim. The sons use the 'bring proof' rule from step 18, and the ספק answers with a 'whichever way' argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ספק says he wins something either way. If he is the יבם's son, he inherits with his brothers. If he is the dead brother's son, he was the only heir, so the half the יבם took was really his. His argument tries to show that his claim is not fully doubtful after all.

keyTerms.meaning: whichever way you want it, either way

steps.confusionAlert: The two halves of the ספק's argument are about different money. The first is a share of the יבם's own estate. The second is the half of the dead brother's estate that the יבם took.

phrases.english: The יבם's sons say:
Bring proof that you are our brother, and take.
The doubtful one said to them:
Whichever way you want it,
if I am your brother
give me a share along with you,
and if I am the dead man's son
give me the half
that your father divided with me.
phrases.notes: If he is the dead man's only son, the half your father took in step 13 should really have been his.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ סָפֵק: מָה נַפְשַׁיְיכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the claims of each side in the case set up in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Presents the claims only. The sons demand proof, and the ספק argues that either way he is owed something. The ruling comes later.

steps.title: Does the first verdict stand or get reopened?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא in the name of רב says the first verdict stands (קם דינא). רבי ירמיה says the verdict goes back and is reopened (הדר דינא).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב: The verdict stands. רבי ירמיה said: The verdict goes back.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about whether the ספק's 'either way' claim works. The question is whether the earlier split of the dead brother's property can be looked at again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to קם דינא, the first split is finished, and the fight over the יבם's estate is judged fresh, so the ספק's argument fails. According to הדר דינא, the first ruling is reopened in light of the new situation. Then the ספק can use what happened in the first split to claim a share now.

keyTerms.meaning: The verdict stands; the earlier ruling is closed
The verdict goes back; the earlier ruling is reopened
An אמורא who holds the ruling is reopened

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions are about the same case from steps 19-20. The only question is whether the old split of the dead brother's property gets reopened when the יבם's estate is divided.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said in the name of Rav:
The verdict stands.
Rabbi Yirmeya said:
The verdict goes back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: קָם דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on whether the ספק's 'either way' claim from step 20 succeeds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the first ruling stays closed, so the ספק gets nothing. רבי ירמיה: the ruling is reopened, so the ספק can claim a share.

steps.title: Is this the same as the argument about a lost path?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי אבא and רבי ירמיה are arguing about the same thing as אדמון and the חכמים. That משנה is about a man who forgot where the path to his field was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say they disagree in the dispute of אדמון and the רבנן, as we learned: One who went overseas and forgot the path to his field. אדמון says he may take the shortest path. The חכמים say he must buy himself a path, even for a hundred מנה, or fly through the air.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that our argument is really an older argument from a משנה. It brings that משנה to set up the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדמון reasons: 'I certainly had a path somewhere, so at least give me the shortest one.' That looks like the ספק's 'either way I deserve something' claim. The חכמים say that without proof of where the path was, he gets nothing for free.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say; introduces a suggested comparison
A judge in ירושלים whose rulings appear in the משנה
Fly through the air; a sharp way of saying 'that's your problem'

phrases.english: Let us say that in the dispute
of Admon and the Rabbis they disagree,
as we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: כתובות 109b

phrases.english: One who went overseas
and the path to his field was lost to him:
phrases.notes: He had a right to a path through other people's land, but he forgot where it ran.

phrases.english: Admon says: He may go by the shortest path.
And the Sages say:
He must buy himself a path, even for a hundred maneh,
phrases.notes: A huge price. He has to pay whatever they ask.

phrases.english: or fly through the air.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּאַדְמוֹן וְרַבָּנַן קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to link the argument in step 21 to an earlier argument in a משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רבי אבא and רבי ירמיה the same as the argument between אדמון and the חכמים?

steps.title: Admon's logic looks strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion of that משנה. There it was asked: אדמון seems right, so how can the חכמים disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: Against the רבנן, אדמון is speaking well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting an earlier discussion of the path משנה. That discussion started with a challenge to the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man surely had a path, so it seems unfair to give him nothing. The challenge asks why the חכמים would deny him at least the shortest one.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it; introduces an earlier discussion
He is speaking well; his argument makes sense

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
Against the Rabbis: Admon is speaking well!
phrases.notes: It's a challenge. Admon's reasoning sounds so right that the Rabbis' view is hard to understand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: לְרַבָּנַן שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר אַדְמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings up an old challenge to the חכמים in the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion of the חכמים in the lost-path משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He certainly had a path somewhere, so at least the shortest path should be his.

steps.title: The field is surrounded by four different owners
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב explains that the field is surrounded on all four sides by four different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: What are we dealing with here? A case where four people surrounded the field from four sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the חכמים by narrowing the case. The field has four separate neighbors, one on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single neighbor can be made to give a path. Each one can say: 'Maybe your path went through someone else's land.' So the man cannot win against any of them.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here; narrows the case

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
What are we dealing with here?
A case where four people surrounded it
from four sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against the חכמים in step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Admon's logic should win, since the man surely had a path.
steps.terutzMaskana: With four different owners, each one can push the claim onto another, so no one has to give a path.

steps.title: Then what is Admon's reason?
steps.stepSummary: If there are four different owners, why would אדמון give the man any path?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is אדמון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the question flips to the other side. The answer that saved the חכמים makes אדמון hard to understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each neighbor can say 'not through my land,' then אדמון's ruling of a shortest path seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; turns the last answer into a new problem

phrases.english: If so,
what is Admon's reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּאַדְמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אדמון's view based on how the case was set up in step 24.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With four separate owners, any one of them can push the man off, so why does אדמון give him a path?

steps.title: Cases where everyone agrees the neighbors win
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that in two cases everyone agrees the neighbors can push the man away. One is four owners who bought from four earlier owners. The other is four owners who bought from one earlier owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: With four who came from four, and four who came from one, everyone agrees that they can push him off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to answer by first listing the cases where אדמון and the חכמים agree. This sets up the case where they really argue, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how the current owners got their land. In these two cases, even אדמון agrees each neighbor can deflect the man's claim. So their argument must be about a different setup.

keyTerms.meaning: Through the rights of; whoever someone got the land from

phrases.english: And Rava said:
With four who came through the rights of four,
phrases.notes: Four current owners, each of whom bought from a different earlier owner.

phrases.english: and four who came through the rights of one,
phrases.notes: Four current owners who all bought from the same single earlier owner.

phrases.english: everyone agrees
that they can push him off.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: בְּאַרְבְּעָה דְּאָתוּ מִכֹּחַ אַרְבְּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question about אדמון's reason in step 25 by first ruling out cases where there is no argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining cases (where everyone agrees, before showing where they argue)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Four owners always means אדמון has no basis.
steps.terutzMaskana: In these two cases everyone agrees the man loses, so the argument must be about some other setup.

steps.title: The real argument: one buyer of all four fields, and אדמון's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא says אדמון and the חכמים argue only when one person bought all four surrounding fields from four earlier owners. אדמון says the man can claim his path from that buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue when one person owns all four fields, having bought them from four different people. אדמון holds that the man can say: Either way, my path is somewhere in your land.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is finishing his answer from the last step. He now names the one case where אדמון and the חכמים really disagree, and gives אדמון's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now one person owns all four sides, so the lost path must be somewhere in his land. That is why אדמון says the man has a real claim against him. In the two cases from step 26 there was no such single person to point at.

keyTerms.meaning: comes on the strength of; holds his rights because he bought from someone
either way; whichever way you look at it

phrases.english: Where they disagree,
is in a case of one person who comes on the strength of four.
phrases.notes: He means one buyer who bought all four surrounding fields from four separate owners.

phrases.english: אדמון holds that he can say to him:
phrases.notes: The man who lost his path is talking to the one buyer.

phrases.english: Either way, my path is with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, בְּחַד דְּאָתֵי מִכֹּחַ אַרְבְּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer by giving the case of disagreement after the two cases of agreement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the argument to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed hard to see why אדמון would give any path when four different people own the land.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only when one buyer holds all four fields that came from four earlier owners. אדמון says that buyer cannot escape the claim.

steps.title: The reason of the חכמים: the buyer can threaten to undo the sales
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the buyer can tell the man to keep quiet. If he does not, the buyer will give the fields back to the four earlier owners, and the man will have no one he can win against.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים hold that the buyer can say: If you keep quiet, fine. If not, I will give the deeds back to the earlier owners, and you will not be able to win a case against them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the other side. He explains why the חכמים say the buyer can still push the man away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer undoes the four sales, we are back to four separate owners. Then each one can say the path is in someone else's field, and the man loses. Because the buyer can make that threat, the man's claim against him is not strong enough.

keyTerms.meaning: the deed or document of sale

steps.whatToRemember: אדמון: one owner of all four sides cannot dodge the claim. The חכמים: he can dodge it by threatening to give the fields back to the four earlier owners.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold that he can say to him:
phrases.notes: Now it is the buyer of the four fields who is talking.

phrases.english: If you keep quiet, keep quiet,
and if not, I will return the deeds to their owners,
and you will not be able to argue a case against them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי שָׁתְקַתְּ — שָׁתְקַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' side of the case that was just defined.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reasoning of the other side
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer's ability to undo the sales protects him, so according to the חכמים the man cannot force him to give a path.

steps.title: Matching רבי אבא to the חכמים and רבי ירמיה to אדמון
steps.stepSummary: Now that the argument is clear, the גמרא finishes its suggestion: רבי אבא follows the חכמים, and רבי ירמיה follows אדמון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבי אבא follows the חכמים, and רבי ירמיה follows אדמון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its suggestion from step 22 and spells out who matches whom. This sets up the next move, where the match will be questioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case, when the man lost his path there were four owners, so at that time he had no claim. Later one buyer bought all four fields. The חכמים say the man still has no claim, so the old outcome stands, like רבי אבא's קם דינא. אדמון says the claim comes back once the situation changes, like רבי ירמיה's הדר דינא.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא may later push back on)
like the Rabbis, here the חכמים of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: לֵימָא is only a suggestion. The גמרא often brings it up and then rejects it, and that is about to happen here.

phrases.english: Shall we say that רבי אבא, who said his ruling, follows the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: His ruling is קם דינא, 'the verdict stands,' from step 21.

phrases.english: And רבי ירמיה, who said his ruling, follows אדמון?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי אַבָּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case defined by רבא to finish the comparison first suggested in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the argument between רבי אבא and רבי ירמיה the same as the argument between the חכמים and אדמון?

steps.title: רבי אבא can fit even with אדמון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. רבי אבא could say his ruling works even for אדמון, because אדמון's reason in the path case was a special either-way argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא could tell you: What I said works even according to אדמון. אדמון only said his ruling there because the man can say: Whichever way you look at it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to reject the match from the last step. It shows that רבי אבא does not have to follow only the חכמים. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא points to אדמון's reason: ממה נפשך, whichever way you look at it, the path is in this buyer's land. That reason may belong only to the path case. If so, אדמון would not have to argue with רבי אבא, and the comparison falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: he could say to you (a defense of a sage's view)
he only said this up to here; limits a ruling to its own case
whichever way you look at it; either way

phrases.english: רבי אבא could say to you:
What I said works even according to אדמון.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר אַדְמוֹן הָתָם,
phrases.english: אדמון only said his ruling there

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: מִמָּה נַפְשָׁךְ
phrases.english: because the man can say to him: Whichever way you look at it

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי אַבָּא: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ כְּאַדְמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion that רבי אבא must follow the חכמים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between רבי אבא and רבי ירמיה and the argument of אדמון and the חכמים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אדמון's ruling rests on a special either-way reason (ממה נפשך) that belongs to the path case. So it does not have to clash with רבי אבא.
